questions.q: Why does Airflow's official install command pin a constraints file, not just the Airflow version?
options: It makes the install run faster
It only affects which Python version you can use, nothing else
It locks every dependency to a version actually tested together, so pip doesn't silently pull in untested combinations
It's a legacy requirement with no current purpose
questions.explain: Airflow has a large dependency tree; the constraints file pins every dependency to versions that were actually tested against that Airflow release.

questions.q: What does the single command `airflow standalone` actually do?
options: Installs Airflow from scratch
Only starts the webserver, nothing else
Deletes all existing DAGs
Initializes the metadata database, creates an admin user, and starts the scheduler, webserver, and triggerer all at once
questions.explain: It's a one-command bootstrap for a complete local Airflow instance — no separate manual setup of each component.

questions.q: Where do you find Airflow's admin password after running `airflow standalone`?
options: It's always printed directly to the terminal with no exceptions
It's the same for every Airflow installation everywhere
In a generated file inside $AIRFLOW_HOME, such as simple_auth_manager_passwords.json.generated
You must set it manually before starting Airflow
questions.explain: In current Airflow versions the password isn't always shown in the terminal — it's saved to a generated file under $AIRFLOW_HOME.

options: A required environment variable that has no default and must always be set manually
The folder (default ~/airflow) holding Airflow's config file, metadata database, and generated credentials
A Python package you must import in every DAG
The URL where the Airflow UI is hosted
questions.explain: $AIRFLOW_HOME defaults to ~/airflow and is where Airflow keeps its configuration and local state.

questions.q: What is an "extra" like the `[celery]` in `apache-airflow[celery]==3.3.1`?
options: A typo that pip ignores
A required flag with no effect on what gets installed
An optional install component in brackets that pulls in additional functionality at install time
A separate, unrelated Python package
questions.explain: Extras in brackets opt into additional functionality (like specific integrations) at install time, on top of the base Airflow install.
